He played [[college basketball]] for the [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC Trojans]] and was selected 26th overall by the [[Chicago Bulls]] in the [[2009 NBA draft]]. A [[power forward]] and [[Center (basketball)|center]], Gibson previously played for the Bulls, [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], [[New York Knicks]], [[Washington Wizards]], [[Detroit Pistons]], and [[Charlotte Hornets]]. ==Early life== Gibson was born on June 24, 1985, in [[Brooklyn|Brooklyn, New York]]. He attended P.S. 67 Charles A. Dorsey School in Brooklyn's [[Fort Greene, Brooklyn|Fort Greene]] neighborhood.{{cite web|last1=Friedell|first1=Nick|title=Representing Brooklyn, Taj Gibson becomes NBA's first No. 67|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/20907635/nba-taj-gibson-chooses-obscure-jersey-number-represent-hometown|website=ESPN|access-date=October 4, 2017|date=October 4, 2017}} Gibson began his high school career at Brooklyn's [[High School of Telecommunication Arts and Technology]]. He then attended Stoneridge Prep as a sophomore and junior in [[Tarzana, California]]. During his senior year in 2006, he attended Calvary Christian in [[San Fernando, California]]. ==College career== [[File:2009-0319-NCAAs-006-TajGibson22.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Gibson during a practice at the NCAA tournament, 2009]] Gibson played at the [[University of Southern California]], where he was a member of the [[Phi Kappa Psi]] fraternity. As one of the oldest freshmen in the country, he was 21 years old in 2007. Gibson was named to the Pac-10 All-Freshman team and helped beat rival [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] in 2008. Gibson was named to the 2009 [[2009 Pacific-10 Conference men's basketball tournament#All-Tournament Team|All-Pac 10 Tournament Team]] by helping the [[USC Trojans|Trojans]] win the [[2009 Pacific-10 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pacific-10 tournament championship]] at the [[Staples Center]].{{Cite web |url=http://blog.pe.com/news/2009/03/14/pac-10-all-tournament-team/ |title=Pac-10 All-Tournament Team |access-date=October 28, 2013 |archive-date=October 29, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029205843/http://blog.pe.com/news/2009/03/14/pac-10-all-tournament-team/ |url-status=dead }} ==Professional career== ===Chicago Bulls (2009–2017)=== Gibson declared for the [[2009 NBA draft]],[https://web.archive.org/web/20131029223548/http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/blog/_/name/katz_andy/id/4107770/sidney-mississippi-state Sidney to Mississippi State?] and was selected 26th overall by the [[Chicago Bulls]]. Along with fellow draft pick [[James Johnson (basketball, born 1987)|James Johnson]], he signed with the Bulls in July 2009.{{cite web | title=Johnson, Gibson sign rookie deals with Bulls | website=ESPN.com | date=2009-07-09 | url=https://www.espn.com/chicago/news/story?id=4317043 | access-date=2025-12-09}} Gibson was the starting power forward for most of his rookie season with the Bulls and impressed many people with his high energy and good defense. During [[2010 NBA All-Star Game|the All-Star Weekend]], Gibson played in the [[NBA All-Star Weekend Rookie Challenge|Rookie Challenge]], where the Rookie team won for the first time since [[2002 NBA All-Star Game|2002]]. The Bulls made the playoffs, securing the 8th seed in the Eastern Conference. Gibson averaged 7.6 points per game and 7.0 rebounds while the Bulls lost to the Cleveland Cavaliers in the first round. At the end of his first season, he was selected to the NBA All-Rookie First Team.[http://www.nba.com/2010/news/04/30/allrookie.2010/ Evans, Jennings, Curry unanimous All-Rookie team picks] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150612045808/http://www.nba.com/2010/news/04/30/allrookie.2010/ |date=June 12, 2015 }} [[File:Taj Gibson Chicago Bulls 2009.jpg|thumb|left|upright=0.85|Gibson with the Bulls in 2009]] During the 2010 off-season, the Bulls signed power forward [[Carlos Boozer]], who was expected to start at the beginning of the season rather than Gibson. But Boozer broke his hand before the pre-season, and Gibson started the first 15 games of the season. After Boozer's return, Gibson moved into a bench role for most of the season. He was selected as a starter for the Sophomore squad in the 2011 NBA Rising Stars challenge at the All-Star weekend, which the Rookie team won 148–140. Gibson played 18 minutes and recorded 8 points.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/allstar/NBA_2011_rookie.html 2011 NBA Rising Stars] At the end of the season, the Bulls made the playoffs as the first seed in the Eastern Conference. On May 10, 2011, Gibson helped his team take a 3–2 lead in the Eastern Conference semifinals against Atlanta, making all of his 11 points in the fourth quarter.[https://web.archive.org/web/20170517190423/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=310510004 Derrick Rose, Bulls put Hawks on brink with dominant fourth] In May 2012, Gibson was named to the US Select Team, joining [[Jeremy Lin]], [[DeMarcus Cousins]], and [[Kyrie Irving]] in practicing with the US Olympic Team in preparation for the [[2012 Summer Olympics]] in London.[https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-gibson-named-usa-mens-select-team.html BULLS' GIBSON NAMED TO USA MEN'S SELECT TEAM] On October 31, 2012, Gibson signed a four-year, $33 million rookie scale contract extension with the Bulls.[https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-taj-gibson-multi-year-extension.html BULLS SIGN TAJ GIBSON TO MULTI-YEAR EXTENSION] Playing mostly a bench role in 2013–14, Gibson averaged 13 points and 6.8 rebounds on the season and was among the league leaders in blocked shots per game. He finished second in the NBA's Sixth Man of the Year Award, losing to [[Jamal Crawford]].[http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/24554353/jamal-crawford-wins-2014-nba-sixth-man-of-the-year Jamal Crawford wins 2014 NBA Sixth Man of the Year] On June 16, 2015, Gibson underwent arthroscopic surgery on his left ankle and was ruled out for four months.[https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/taj-gibson-injury-update TAJ GIBSON INJURY UPDATE] During the [[2015–16 NBA season|2015–16 season]], he appeared in 73 games and averaged 8.6 points and 6.9 rebounds.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/gibsota01.html Taj Gibson]. web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/gibson-mcdermott-170223|title=Thunder Acquires Gibson, McDermott and Draft Pick|work=NBA.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 23, 2017}} 67,{{cite web|title=NBA & ABA Players Who Wore Uniform Number 67|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/friv/numbers.fcgi?number=67 |website=Basketball-Reference|access-date=February 3, 2022}} in Gibson signed a 10-day contract with Detroit on March 6.|number=1769062557245964335|user=Pistons_PR|date=March 16, 2024|access-date=March 16, 2024}} Gibson made four appearances for Detroit, averaging 4.5 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 0.5 assists.{{Cite web|title=Taj Gibson 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3986/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Charlotte Hornets (2024–2025)=== On July 13, 2024, Gibson signed a one-year, $3.3 million contract with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|title=Hornets Sign Taj Gibson|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-sign-taj-gibson|website=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2024|access-date=July 13, 2024}} On April 9, 2025, Gibson played his 1,000th NBA game, in a loss to the [[2024–25 Toronto Raptors season|Toronto Raptors]]. He finished with two points and five rebounds in 16 minutes off the bench.{{cite web|title=Nick Smith Jr. Has Career Night, Raptors Roar Past Hornets In 2nd Half|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/nick-smith-jr-has-career-night-raptors-roar-past-hornets-in-2nd-half|website=NBA.com|date=April 9, 2025|access-date=April 9, 2025}} Gibson made 37 total appearances (including 11 starts) for Charlotte during the regular season, posting averages of 2.9 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 0.6 assists.{{Cite web|title=Taj Gibson 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3986/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2026–present)=== On February 26, 2026, Gibson
